key_features.classic_presentation: ONSET: SUDDEN onset during trauma - fall on outstretched arm, direct blow, or forceful abduction/external rotation. LOCATION: Anterior shoulder (95% anterior dislocations), posterior shoulder (5% posterior dislocations). DURATION: Immediate severe pain that persists until reduction. CHARACTER: SEVERE, SHARP, CONSTANT pain. AGGRAVATING: ANY shoulder movement, especially abduction and external rotation. RELIEVING: NOTHING relieves pain until reduction. Patient holds arm in protective position. TIMING: Immediate severe pain that persists until reduction. SEVERITY: 8-10/10, severe and unrelenting. ASSOCIATED SYMPTOMS: OBVIOUS DEFORMITY (squared-off shoulder, prominent acromion), arm held in abduction and external rotation, inability to move shoulder, numbness/tingling in arm (axillary nerve injury), 'dead arm' sensation. May have audible 'pop' at injury. KEY POSITIVES: Obvious deformity, positive apprehension test, positive relocation test, axillary nerve deficit, prominent acromion. KEY NEGATIVES: No bony tenderness over clavicle or humerus (rules out fracture), no crepitus.

red_flags: Open wound with bone visible - open dislocation, call 911
Severe neurovascular compromise - cold, pale, pulseless arm, call 911
Associated fracture - humeral head or glenoid fracture, needs urgent orthopedic evaluation
Recurrent dislocations with minimal trauma - possible chronic instability
Elderly patients - higher risk of associated fractures and complications
